standard_prerequisites: the dilatations theorem (theorem-dilatations-general of the same chapter) and its correspondence between f : X' -> X and g : W -> X_{/T}
quasi-separatedness of f implies quasi-separatedness of g (lemma-quasi-separated-gives-quasi-separated of the same chapter)

quasi-separatedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces checked etale locally on the base (Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-separated-local; Formal Spaces, Lemma formal-spaces-lemma-separated-local)
quasi-compactness of fibre products for quasi-separated W and the identification (V_j x V_{j'})_{/T} = (V_j)_{/T} x_{X'_{/T}} (V_{j'})_{/T}
a formal algebraic space is quasi-compact if and only if its associated reduced algebraic space is quasi-compact
core_obligations: Prove that in the situation of the dilatations theorem, f : X' -> X is quasi-separated if and only if g : W -> X_{/T} is quasi-separated
proof_roadmap: Conversely, quasi-separatedness of f is checked etale locally on X over affines, so one reduces to X affine Noetherian with U' -> U an isomorphism.

For a surjective etale V -> X' with V a disjoint union of affines V_j, the fibre products (V_j x V_{j'})_{/T} are quasi-compact because W is quasi-separated, the open part (V_j x_{X'} V_{j'}) x_X U is quasi-compact, and the topological space of V_j x_{X'} V_{j'} is the disjoint union of the open part and the reduced formal part, whence V_j x_{X'} V_{j'} is quasi-compact and X' is quasi-separated.
difficulty_reason: H3: an etale-local reduction plus a topological decomposition argument, each ingredient standard.
